summary: Wilde's friendship with Adela Schuster on its ordinary footing in December 1894, months before the trials — she later gave him £1,000.
certainty_reasoning: The record documents a friendship or acquaintance with no evidence of attraction or romance; classified platonic, upgradable if contrary evidence comes to light.

sources.quote: Dear Miss Schuster, I was so sorry I could not come down yesterday: but I will try and come down for the afternoon next Sunday: I was so pleased at all you said of the Woman of No Importance. My new play the Ideal Husband - to be brought out in January - I like less - there is no one like myself in it - horrid objective creations of serious folk. However it has some dramatic scenes in it. Sincerely yours
sources.context: Wilde to Adela Schuster, [? December 1894], 16 Tite Street (MS Hyde) - quoted whole. Four months before the trials. 'there is no one like myself in it' is Wilde on An Ideal Husband, and is as good a statement of his own measure of a play as he gives anywhere.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The friendship at its ordinary footing, months before she gave him £1,000.

manuscript.repository: British Library, London (Lady Eccles Oscar Wilde Collection)
